step1_analysis.description: A 4-input analog summing amplifier used to realize an analog implementation of an FM differential equation at baseband. It uses four parallel common-source NMOS transistors to convert input voltages to currents, which are summed and converted back to a voltage by an NMOS enhancement (diode-connected) load.

paper_reference.title: An Analog GFSK Modulator in 0.35-um CMOS

VOUT_DC.description: DC Output Voltage at the operating point

sky130_expected.calculation: Equating the sum of currents from XM1-XM4 (in linear region due to high Vgs=0.9V and low Vds) to the current of the diode-connected XM5 load. 4 * un*Cox*(W/L)*[(Vgs-Vth)*VOUT - 0.5*VOUT^2] = 0.5*un*Cox*(W/L)*(VDD-VOUT-Vth5)^2. Solving with VDD=1.8V gives VOUT ~ 0.3V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the ratio of the pull-down network strength to the pull-up load strength.

Gain.description: Small-Signal Voltage Gain from one input to output

sky130_expected.calculation: Av = -gm1 / (gm5 + gds_total). gm1 ~ 0.8mS, gm5 ~ 2.4mS, gds_total ~ 1.9mS. Av ~ -0.8 / 4.3 = -0.18 V/V, which is ~ -15 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The circuit acts as an attenuating summer, which is common in baseband analog processing to prevent clipping when summing multiple large signals.

sky130_expected.calculation: f3dB = Gout / (2*pi*Cout). With Gout ~ 4.3mS and Cout ~ 50fF, f3dB ~ 13 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Very wideband due to the low impedance of the diode-connected load (1/gm5). It easily covers the required baseband frequencies (160kHz - 1.5MHz).
Matches the paper's reported 600uA from a 3V supply (1.8mW) for the modulator core.

THD.description: Total Harmonic Distortion for a 0.1V amplitude input

sky130_expected.calculation: Non-linearity of the NMOS transistors in the linear region introduces harmonics. For a 0.1V swing on a 0.9V bias, THD is typically low.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 1% and 3% metrics which likely correspond to modulation error or THD.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, small-signal gain, bandwidth, and THD of the analog summing amplifier.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Analog Summing Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

XM2 VOUT IN1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VOUT IN2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUT IN3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM1 VOUT IN4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM5 VDD VDD VOUT GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VIN1 IN1 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.1 1MEG 0 0)
VIN2 IN2 0 DC 0.9 AC 0
VIN3 IN3 0 DC 0.9 AC 0
VIN4 IN4 0 DC 0.9 AC 0

Cload VOUT 0 50f

.control
* Operating Point
op
print v(VOUT)
let pwr = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print pwr

* AC Analysis
ac dec 10 1k 100G
let gain_db = vdb(VOUT)
meas ac midband_gain find gain_db at=100k
meas ac gain_10G find gain_db at=10G

* Transient Analysis for THD
tran 10n 5u
meas tran vout_pk2pk pp v(VOUT)
fourier 1MEG v(VOUT)

quit
.endc
.end
